cityQuote: God’s blessing on all nations, who long and work for that bright day, when o’er earth’s habitations no war, no strife shall hold its sway.
cityQuoteAttribution: France Prešeren, “Zdravljica” (“A Toast”), 1844. This verse is Slovenia’s national anthem.
heroTitle: Ljubljana hero — Med Cruise Guide (CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons)
wordsPreamble:
- Slovene is spoken by about two million people. Almost everyone in Ljubljana under 50 speaks good English.
- Č is “ch,” š is “sh,” ž is “zh,” c is “ts,” and j is “y.” The l at the end of a syllable often sounds like “w.”
- Slovene keeps the dual: separate word forms for exactly two of something, which very few languages still have.
- Ljubljana is said “lyoo-BLYAH-nah.” The old German name was Laibach.
